definitions.explanation: A round, hollow Japanese doll modeled after Bodhidharma, the founder of Zen Buddhism. Traditionally painted red with a bearded face, the doll is designed as a tumbler that always rights itself when knocked over. Used for goal-setting and as a good luck charm.

examples.japanese: {願|ねが}いを{込|こ}めてだるまの{片目|かため}を{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I painted in one eye of the daruma while making a wish.

examples.japanese: {選挙|せんきょ}に{当選|とうせん}したので、だるまにもう{片方|かたほう}の{目|め}を{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I filled in the other eye of the daruma because I won the election.

examples.japanese: だるまは{七転|ななころ}び{八起|やお}きの{象徴|しょうちょう}だ。
examples.english: The daruma is a symbol of perseverance (falling seven times and getting up eight).

notes:
ALTERNATE WRITING:
・{達磨|だるま} (kanji form)

ORIGIN:
・Named after {達磨|だるま} (Bodhidharma), who supposedly meditated for nine years until his arms and legs atrophied
・This explains the doll's armless, legless round shape

TRADITIONAL USE:
1. Buy a daruma with blank white eyes
2. Make a wish/goal and paint in the LEFT eye ({左目|ひだりめ})
3. When the goal is achieved, paint in the RIGHT eye ({右目|みぎめ})
4. At year's end, return to a temple for {だるま}{供養|くよう} (ritual burning)

PROVERB:
・{七転|ななころ}び{八起|やお}き (Fall seven times, rise eight) - the tumbler design embodies this spirit of resilience

FAMOUS PRODUCTION AREAS:
・{高崎|たかさき}だるま (Takasaki, Gunma) - most famous
・{白河|しらかわ}だるま (Shirakawa, Fukushima)

COLORS:
・{赤|あか} (red) - traditional, good luck
・{白|しろ} (white) - academic success
・{金|きん} (gold) - financial success
・Various modern colors available

MODERN USE:
・Politicians display them during election campaigns
・Athletes and students use them for goal motivation
・Popular as New Year decorations

COLLOCATIONS:
・だるまに{目|め}を{入|い}れる (to paint daruma's eye)
・だるま{落|お}とし (daruma drop game)
